title: Brief Announcement: Delay-Optimal Transaction Order Fairness
venue: ACM Symposium on Principles of Distributed Computing
summary: Characterizes achievable approximate transaction order fairness under synchrony, relating the receipt-time gap to the fraction of nodes supporting an ordering constraint.
note: PODC 2026 brief announcement. The linked full version contains the extended analysis and proofs.
abstract: Approximate order fairness requires one transaction to precede another when enough nodes report receiving it sufficiently earlier. The full paper studies this requirement using physical receipt times in a synchronous network with Byzantine faults. It identifies parameter regions where conflicting ordering constraints cannot form a cycle and gives protocols that choose a receipt-gap guarantee from the reported transaction profile. The guarantees depend on the stated synchrony and clock model.
